corpus: original model suggestions with verified insertion in earlier sessions
finding: No useful primary personal advantage is established. Useful base and pooled advantage is excluded under writer resampling but remains unresolved under crossed resampling. Donor advantage is excluded under both interval methods; uniform advantage remains unresolved under both, including its writer lower endpoint just beyond the useful margin. All primary intervals include zero. Adapted-minus-base donor useful advantage is excluded under writer resampling but remains unresolved under crossed resampling; pooled advantage remains unresolved under both. Residual uniform useful advantage is excluded under both methods, with worse performance at zero only under writer resampling; all residual model-rival intervals include zero. Raw sums retain useful base, pooled and donor uncertainty under both methods, with all model-rival intervals including zero. Raw sums are worse than uniform under both methods. No parity follows.
limits: Repeated selected model text adds training passes, not personal evidence. Suggestion supply and selection provenance, sparse histories, fixed donor/global training, shared exposed units and changed corpus support preclude epoch/backbone/corpus rankings, independent human confirmation, population limits, private-goal inference or a whole-matrix verdict. Historical failures and unknown attempts stay separate; no new retry.
